image_description: A close-up side view of a butterfly resting on a textured gray surface (likely stone or concrete). The butterfly has orange-brown wings with visible eyespots (ocelli) featuring red and blue centers. The body is slender and brown. Antennae are long, thin, and clubbed at the tips. Legs are visible gripping the surface.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The antennae are clearly visible, extending forward and upward, with distinct thickened clubs at the distal ends, matching the Nymphalidae characteristic.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Satyrid butterfly with moderately sized wingspan.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The subject is clearly a butterfly. While exact wingspan cannot be measured without scale, the proportions relative to the body and the visible wing section are consistent with a medium-sized satyrid like a ringlet.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Wings uniformly brown to dark brown with small eyespots (ocelli) arranged in rows.

While eyespots are present, the base coloration deviates significantly from the 'dark brown' description typical of the ventral side of a Ringlet (Aphantopus hyperantus), suggesting either a different species (e.g., Meadow Brown) or an AI color hallucination.

The visible legs (mid and hind) appear somewhat spindly and lack clear joint segmentation. The connection point of the hind leg to the thorax is slightly ambiguous/mushy.
The base of the antennae seems to emerge from the head without a clear socket or pedicel structure, blending slightly into the head capsule.
